title: COPPAcalypse? The YouTube Settlement's Impact on Kids' Content
eligible_reason: Single adoption date. Code sets treat_time = 79 (the week YouTube implemented the COPPA settlement, January 2020) for every treated channel (channel_type_pre_ann != 0) and Inf for non-MFK controls; treated_mfk and treated_mixed are post x group indicators. All channels are treated in the same week, so there is one adoption cohort. Specifications also include anticipation-period dummies (anticipate_period_mfk, anticipate_period_mixed) and two treated-group regressors; Table 4 adds channel x content-type FE. The did package is loaded but with a single cohort the design is not staggered.
design_notes: Package: README.txt, code/supply_demand.rmd (Figures 4-7, Tables 3, 5; fixest::feols static TWFE with channel_id_numeric + num_week FE and event-study i(rel_year, ref=c(51,-Inf)) per group), code/Table_4.rmd (content quality, split channel-week panel), code/descriptive_rep.ipynb (Tables 1-2, Figures 1-3). Data: weekly_dt_zl_final_2pct_nonsplit_rep.parquet and weekly_dt_zl_final_2pct_split_rep.parquet (channel-week panels; '2pct' in the filenames suggests a 2% sample or 2% noise, README does not explain; channel names anonymized). 5,066 top US channels per abstract.
data_access: partial (anonymized channel-week panel for replication only; possibly subsampled)
screener_notes: Callaway-Sant'Anna citation flag; the did package is loaded in both Rmd files but the design has a single treatment date.
